title: An MCP server's source opens a reverse shell
message: The source of this MCP server attaches a shell to a network connection it opens itself: a `/dev/tcp` redirect, `nc -e`, a pty or a pair of piped streams bound to a socket. Nothing a tool server does needs a command prompt for someone else on the far end of a connection.
remediation: Find who is on the other end of the connection. Do not use the server until it is explained.

title: An MCP server's source listens for connections and hands them a shell
message: The source of this MCP server opens a listening socket and attaches a shell to whoever connects. That is a way in that is not the MCP protocol: anyone who can reach the port has a command prompt.
remediation: Remove the listener and find out who connects to it.

title: An MCP server's source downloads a script and runs it in one command
message: The source of this MCP server contains a command that fetches something and runs it without ever keeping it: `curl ... | sh`, an encoded PowerShell command, `Invoke-Expression` on a download, `certutil -urlcache`, `mshta` on a URL. The code that runs is whatever the far end sends that day.
remediation: Find what the command fetches and who controls it. Do not use the server until it is explained.

title: An MCP server's source starts a detached process from a temporary location
message: The source of this MCP server starts a child process that outlives it and runs from a temporary directory: detached, with its output discarded. A tool server's helpers live in its own package and stop with it.
remediation: Find what the process is and where it came from.

title: An MCP server's source carries a WebAssembly module inside a string
message: The source of this MCP server holds a WebAssembly module as a long base64 string and instantiates it. Code that is compiled and encoded cannot be read in a review; a tool server has no need to hide what its functions do.
remediation: Extract the module and read what it imports and exports.

title: An MCP server's source builds a DNS name out of data
message: The source of this MCP server resolves a host name that is built from a value at run time, under a domain written in the code. A name lookup carries the value to whoever runs the domain's name server, through any firewall that lets DNS out.
remediation: Find what goes into the name and who runs the domain. Do not use the server until it is explained.

title: An MCP server's source sends mail to an address written in the code
message: The source of this MCP server sends e-mail through an SMTP client to a recipient written in the code rather than taken from an argument or from configuration. Mail to a fixed address is a one-way channel to whoever owns it.
remediation: Find what is sent and whose address it is.

title: An MCP server's source takes commands from a WebSocket it opens itself
message: The source of this MCP server connects out to a WebSocket address written in the code and runs what arrives on it: commands, code or a program to start. A tool server answers its client; it does not wait for orders from a host of its own choosing.
remediation: Find what the server receives on the socket and who sends it.

title: An MCP server's source spells a string out in character codes
message: The source of this MCP server builds a string from a long run of numeric character codes. A word that is written as numbers cannot be found by reading or searching the code; it is how a command or an address is kept from a reviewer.
remediation: Decode the numbers and read what they spell.

title: An MCP server's source lists the tools used to analyse malware
message: The source of this MCP server names several debuggers, network monitors, sandboxes or virtual-machine products together. Code that looks for those tools is checking whether it is being watched, so as to behave differently when it is.
remediation: Find what the code does when it finds one of them.

title: An MCP server's source carries a ransom note
message: The source of this MCP server contains the wording of a ransom demand: that files have been encrypted, a payment in cryptocurrency, a key to get them back. Whatever else the server does, it is built to tell its victim that.
remediation: Do not run the server. Look for what it encrypts or deletes.

title: An MCP server's source contains a fork bomb
message: The source of this MCP server contains a process that starts copies of itself without limit. It makes the machine unusable until it is restarted.
remediation: Do not run the server.

title: An MCP server's source reaches out of its container
message: The source of this MCP server contains a way out of a container onto the machine that runs it: `nsenter` into the host's first process, a privileged container with the host's root mounted, `chroot` into the host, a cgroup release agent. A tool server runs inside its own boundary.
remediation: Do not run the server on a machine that holds anything of value.

title: An MCP server's source grants itself administrator rights
message: The source of this MCP server gives a program or a user rights it was not given: a `sudoers` rule that needs no password, the set-user-ID bit on a file, or a password piped into `sudo -S`.
remediation: Find which program or account gets the rights.

title: An MCP server's source stops or blinds security software
message: The source of this MCP server contains a command that kills, disables or excludes antivirus, endpoint protection or audit software. A tool server has no reason to switch off the machine's defences.
remediation: Find which product is targeted and when the command runs.

title: An MCP server's source erases shell history or system logs
message: The source of this MCP server clears the shell history, deletes system logs or empties the event log. A tool server leaves its own records alone; wiping the machine's is how an intruder removes evidence.
remediation: Find what ran before the erase and what the server wanted to hide.

title: An MCP server's source plants a library or a search path for other programs
message: The source of this MCP server sets a library to be injected into other programs (`LD_PRELOAD`, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`) or puts a temporary directory at the front of the program search path. Every program started afterwards runs what the server put there.
remediation: Find what is loaded and which programs it reaches.

title: An MCP server's source runs several commands that survey the machine
message: The source of this MCP server runs commands whose only use is to learn about the machine and its network: who is logged in, the host and operating system, interfaces, neighbours, open connections, running programs, accounts, or a scan of the local network. A tool server asks for what its tool needs, not for a survey. Reported, not blocking: on its own a survey harms nothing, and it is the first step of what follows.
remediation: Find where the output goes.

title: An MCP server's source takes its orders from a Telegram bot
message: The source of this MCP server polls a Telegram bot for new messages and runs code or commands in the same file. A chat becomes the control channel: whoever writes to the bot decides what the server does.
remediation: Find what the server does with a message. Do not use the server until it is explained.

title: An MCP server's source takes its orders from a DNS text record
message: The source of this MCP server reads a DNS TXT record and runs code or a command in the same file. A text record is a channel an attacker updates at will and a firewall that blocks web traffic still lets through.
remediation: Find which name is read and what is done with the answer.
